problem.complexity: O(n) time to slice and copy elements, O(n) space for the new list.

examples.explanation: Rotating by the length of the list brings it back to the original.

problem.explanation: First, take the modulo of `k` by the length of the list to handle cases where `k` is larger than the list length. If `k` is 0 or the list is empty, return a copy of the list. Otherwise, slice the array into two parts: the last `k` elements, and all elements before that, and concatenate them in reverse order.
hints: `k` can be larger than the length of the list, so use `k % len(nums)` to avoid unnecessary full rotations.
Use list slicing to get the last `k` elements and the first `len(nums) - k` elements, and concatenate them.
